label: Chapter 4: The night the saints fell

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Real history now. No jokes?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: No jokes. Not for this one, and not for the next.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Understood.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In the summer of 1566, a wave of attacks on Catholic churches swept the Low Countries.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's called the Beeldenstorm, which means the storm of images.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: People smashed statues, altars and church fittings.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Why?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was part of the religious conflict of the Reformation.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Some Protestants considered religious images idolatry.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And it reached Antwerp.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: On 20 August 1566. The Cathedral of Our Lady was badly damaged inside.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: An English merchant, Richard Clough, was there.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He wrote that the church looked like a hell, with above 10,000 torches burning.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's a line you don't forget.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's one reason this night is remembered.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Statues fell. Organs were wrecked.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Books were burned.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the building today? It looks perfect.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It survived, and was repaired, and it survived more.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1794, French revolutionary troops plundered it and did serious damage.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Around 1798 the French authorities even planned to demolish it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was spared.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the cathedral itself has one more odd feature.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The towers. Two were planned, equal in height.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Only the north tower was finished, rising 123 meters.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A fire in 1533 delayed the second, and it was never completed.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's lopsided on purpose?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: On purpose is too strong. It's lopsided because of fire, money and time.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the well?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Next to the cathedral on the Handschoenmarkt there's an ornate iron well cover, from the 1500s.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is traditionally attributed to Quinten Matsys, the artist.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Only traditionally. I couldn't confirm it from a firm source.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Tradition again.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's that kind of city.
